md_description: This DAG represents an in vivo mouse cortex electrophysiology workflow using multielectrode array recordings during behavioral tasks. It captures raw local field potential and spike-related signals, processes them into analysis-ready neural features, and integrates them with stimulus parameters and behavioral annotations. The resulting derivatives support dataset metadata generation and downstream analysis of neural correlates of decision-making.

mouse.reasoning: The mouse node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic biological/source metadata: subject identity/biological attributes, provenance, and origin relevant to an in vivo mouse cortex recording. I excluded anything about preparation, recording settings, signals, or computed outputs because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/subject identifiers that are commonly generated at the root across the DAG if they might overlap with already_generated fields, and kept the schema focused on mouse-specific intrinsic descriptors needed to interpret the source animal.

md_schema.descr: Biological species of the subject mouse used as the source animal for the in vivo cortical electrophysiology session; use a controlled taxon label such as Mus musculus.
Mouse strain or line used for the recording subject, recorded as the vendor or colony designation at enrollment; example values include C57BL/6J, BALB/c, or transgenic line names.
Sex of the mouse subject at the time of recording; record the biological sex used in study design and analysis.
Age of the mouse subject in weeks at the time of recording or preparation; typical range for adult in vivo electrophysiology mice is roughly 6 to 20 weeks.
Body weight of the mouse in grams measured at or immediately before the recording-preparation stage; typical range is approximately 15 to 40 g depending on age and strain.
Genetic background or line context of the mouse subject, including any transgene or knockout status if applicable; record the designation used by the colony or vendor.
Origin of the mouse subject, such as vendor, institutional colony, or breeding colony name; use this to document provenance of the animal before any surgical or recording preparation.
Observed health status of the mouse prior to recording preparation, as assessed by the experimenter; use a study-specific categorical label such as healthy, mildly compromised, or excluded.

Unique identifier for the mouse subject used in this experiment; use a stable string identifier such as mouse_001. If a root-level subject identifier already exists in already_generated, do not repeat it here.

recording_preparation.reasoning: The recording_preparation node is a Process, so I included only how the preparation was performed: surgical/physical setup parameters, anesthesia or analgesia if used, site preparation, mounting/stabilization details, and immediate prep quality indicators. I excluded mouse intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded capture/instrument settings and raw data properties because those belong to the downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated field names or semantically equivalent subject descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Type of preparation performed before multielectrode cortical recording, recorded at the start of the prep step; use this to distinguish surgical implantation, acute craniotomy, head-fixation setup, or other physical setup.
Whether anesthesia was administered during the preparation step; record the study-specific decision used immediately before or during the surgical/physical setup.
Anesthetic agent used during recording preparation, if applicable; examples include isoflurane, ketamine/xylazine, or other protocol-specific agents.
Whether analgesia was administered as part of the preparation workflow, recorded at prep time when surgical manipulation is involved.
Analgesic compound used during preparation, if applicable; record the exact agent used in the surgery or setup protocol, such as buprenorphine.

Total duration of the recording preparation step in minutes, measured from the start of setup to the point the mouse is ready for capture; typical range may be roughly 10 to 180 minutes depending on protocol complexity.
Method used to gain access for cortical recording during preparation; record the physical setup approach used to expose or access cortex before capture, such as craniotomy or through-skull recording.
Whether a head-fixation or restraint apparatus was installed or configured during preparation for the recording session.
Anatomical cortical site prepared for the recording session, described at the preparation stage; example entries include primary motor cortex, primary visual cortex, or custom atlas labels.

Immediate quality assessment of the preparation before capture begins, indicating whether the animal and recording site were ready for multielectrode measurement; use a study-defined categorical label.

prepared_mouse.reasoning: I corrected the collision by removing subject_id, since subject/sample identifiers are generated once at the root Entity and must not repeat in downstream nodes. The remaining fields stay within the prepared_mouse Entity territory by describing the post-preparation state of the mouse and its readiness for recording, without drifting into preparation procedure details, capture settings, or signal/output metadata.

md_schema.descr: Overall condition of the mouse immediately after recording setup and before cortical electrophysiology begins; use this to summarize whether the subject is stable and ready for the behavioral recording session.
Status of any recording implant, headcap, or head-fixation hardware after preparation is complete; record whether the setup is present and usable for the upcoming capture session.
Whether the mouse is in a state suitable for behavioral task performance during the upcoming electrophysiology session; record the readiness at the point the prepared mouse is handed off to capture.

Time in minutes allowed or observed between completion of preparation and start of electrophysiological capture, measured at the handoff between preparation and recording; typical values may range from 0 to 240 minutes depending on protocol.
Free-text note summarizing any stable caveats about the prepared mouse before capture, such as residual sedation, reduced mobility, or minor handling issues observed after setup.

cortical_ephys_capture.reasoning: The cortical_ephys_capture node is a Capture, so I included only measurement-session and instrument-configuration metadata: the multielectrode array hardware identity, channel configuration, sampling/acquisition settings, reference/gain configuration, and capture-quality indicators. I excluded mouse attributes and preparation details because those belong to upstream Entity/Process nodes, and I excluded file format, path, size, and raw signal dimensions because those belong to downstream Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any previously generated fields, including subject identifiers and any raw-data descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the multielectrode array system used during cortical electrophysiology capture; record the hardware vendor at the time of the session.
Model name or number of the multielectrode array system configured for the recording session; use the exact device model used to acquire the raw cortical signals.
Serial number of the multielectrode array system used for capture, recorded from the instrument label or device record; use a stable string identifier such as SN12345.
Type or family of multielectrode array used for cortical capture, recorded at session setup; examples include planar array, silicon probe, or tetrode-based array as applicable to the experiment.
Number of active recording channels configured for the capture session, measured at acquisition start; typical values depend on the array and may range from a few channels to hundreds.
Analog-to-digital sampling rate in hertz used during the cortical recording session; record the acquisition rate configured on the instrument at capture time, commonly in the kHz range.
Input amplification or gain setting applied by the acquisition system during capture, recorded at the start of the session; use the instrument-specific numeric gain value.
Reference electrode or grounding configuration used for the recording session, as set on the acquisition hardware before data collection.
Date-time when the cortical electrophysiology capture session began, recorded at the start of acquisition for this mouse behavioral task.
Immediate quality assessment of the capture session based on signal stability and acquisition integrity during recording; use a study-defined categorical label.

raw_lfp_signal.reasoning: For the raw_lfp_signal Signal node, I kept only raw artefact properties and removed the colliding channel_count field because it had already been generated earlier in the DAG. The remaining fields describe the stored LFP object itself: format, location, size, duration, sample count, timing resolution, amplitude units, and a technical integrity flag. I excluded capture settings, filtering, features, and interpretation because those belong to upstream Capture or downstream Process/Derivative nodes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw local field potential signal artefact as stored after capture; record the exact technical format used for the raw data file, such as .abf, .nwb, .bin, or .mat.
Storage location or path for the raw LFP file, recorded as a string path or URI to the artefact in the data repository; example: s3://bucket/session1/raw_lfp.nwb.
Size of the raw LFP data file in bytes measured after capture and storage; typical values vary widely with recording duration and channel count.
Duration of the raw LFP time series in seconds represented by the file, measured from the start to end of the captured electrophysiology trace; typical ranges may span minutes to hours.
Total number of time samples in the raw LFP time series file, measured for the stored artefact; this describes the raw data dimensions rather than the acquisition settings.
Temporal resolution between consecutive LFP samples in seconds, derived from the stored raw signal timing information; for evenly sampled data this is the inverse of the sampling rate.
Physical units used to store raw LFP amplitudes in the file, such as microvolts; record the unit attached to the raw signal values.
Technical quality assessment of the raw LFP artefact, such as whether the file is complete and readable or affected by corruption or missing segments; use a controlled categorical label.

raw_spike_signal.reasoning: The raw_spike_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw artefact descriptors specific to the spike-bearing voltage time series: file format, storage location, file size, duration, dimensionality, amplitude units, and technical quality. I excluded capture configuration and mouse/preparation details because those belong upstream, and I excluded spike sorting outputs or interpretation because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided previously generated fields, including any reused channel-count descriptor, by focusing on signal-object properties not yet named elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw spike-bearing voltage signal artefact as stored after capture; record the exact technical format used for the raw data file, such as .abf, .nwb, .bin, or .mat.
Storage location or path for the raw spike signal file, recorded as a string path or URI to the artefact in the data repository; example: s3://bucket/session1/raw_spike_signal.nwb.
Size of the raw spike signal file in bytes measured after capture and storage; typical values depend on channel count, sample rate, and recording duration.
Duration of the raw spike-bearing time series in seconds represented by the file, measured from the start to end of the captured voltage trace; typical ranges may span minutes to hours.
Total number of time samples in the raw spike signal file, measured for the stored artefact; this describes the raw data dimensions rather than acquisition settings.

Temporal resolution between consecutive samples in seconds for the raw spike-bearing voltage trace, derived from the stored signal timing information; for evenly sampled data this is the inverse of the sampling rate.
Physical units used to store raw spike signal amplitudes in the file, such as microvolts; record the unit attached to the raw voltage values.
Technical quality assessment of the raw spike artefact, such as whether the file is complete and readable or affected by corruption, clipping, or missing segments; use a controlled categorical label.

signal_filtering.reasoning: The signal_filtering node is a Process, so I included only how the filtering/conditioning was performed: software agent identity, filter types, band definitions, order, notch settings, and output-quality indicators for the processing step. I excluded raw and filtered signal file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal and downstream Signal nodes, and I excluded biological or session-level capture settings because those are outside this process's territory. I also avoided duplicate field names from earlier nodes and kept the schema focused on algorithmic/protocol parameters needed to reproduce the filtering step.

md_schema.descr: Software package used to perform electrophysiology signal filtering, recorded for the process step; example names include Python-based workflows or dedicated neural signal tools.
Version of the filtering software used during signal conditioning, recorded exactly as installed or executed for this process; example: 1.2.3.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used for the filtering process, recorded to support reproducibility of the signal-conditioning step.
Type of filter applied to the raw electrophysiology signals during conditioning; examples include bandpass, highpass, lowpass, notch, or combined filtering.
Lower cutoff frequency in hertz for the filtering operation, measured or configured during the signal_filtering step; typical values depend on whether the target is LFP or spike activity.
Upper cutoff frequency in hertz for the filtering operation, measured or configured during the signal_filtering step; typical values depend on whether the target is LFP or spike activity.
Mains or interference rejection frequency in hertz used during filtering, if a notch filter was applied; common values are 50 or 60 Hz depending on region.
Order of the digital filter applied during signal conditioning, recorded at the point of processing; this parameter affects the steepness and phase characteristics of the filter.
Immediate quality indicator for the filtered output generated by the process, summarizing whether filtering succeeded without obvious artefacts or instability; use a controlled label.

filtered_lfp.reasoning: The filtered_lfp node is a Signal, so I included only stored signal-object descriptors for the filtered LFP artefact: file format, location, size, dimensions, units, and signal-specific technical quality. I excluded filtering parameters because those belong to the upstream signal_filtering Process, and I excluded features or alignment results because those belong to downstream Derivative/Process nodes. I also avoided any previously generated field names, including general file and duration descriptors where they would collide with earlier raw-signal fields, and instead used filtered-LFP-specific names.

md_schema.descr: File format of the filtered local field potential artefact as stored after signal conditioning; record the exact technical format used for the filtered data file, such as .abf, .nwb, .bin, or .mat.
Storage location or path for the filtered LFP file, recorded as a string path or URI to the artefact in the data repository; example: s3://bucket/session1/filtered_lfp.nwb.
Size of the filtered LFP file in bytes measured after processing and storage; this captures the stored artefact size rather than raw recording size.
Total number of time samples in the filtered LFP artefact, measured for the stored signal object; this describes the processed signal dimensions.

Temporal resolution between consecutive samples in seconds for the filtered LFP trace, derived from the stored artefact timing information; for evenly sampled data this is the inverse of the effective sampling rate.
Physical units used to store filtered LFP amplitudes in the file, such as microvolts; record the unit attached to the processed signal values.
Technical quality assessment of the filtered LFP artefact, such as whether the file is complete, readable, and free of obvious processing failure; use a controlled categorical label.

spike_sorting.reasoning: The spike_sorting node is a Process, so I included only algorithmic and workflow parameters: sorter software identity, version, repository/pipeline, detection and clustering settings, and summary quality indicators for the sorting operation. I excluded raw spike file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting spike train representation because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any already-generated software fields from other processes by using spike-sorting-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Name of the spike sorting software or algorithm used to detect and separate putative neuronal spikes from the raw spike-bearing signal; example tools include Kilosort, MountainSort, or SpikeInterface-based workflows.
Version of the spike sorting software used for the sorting process, recorded exactly as executed; example: 2.5.0.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used to run spike sorting, recorded to support reproducibility of the sorting step.

Spike detection threshold expressed in standard deviations of the noise estimate used by the sorter, measured or configured during the spike_sorting step; typical values are often between 3 and 6 sigma.
Method used to cluster detected spike events into units during spike sorting; examples include template matching, density-based clustering, or manual curation.
Estimated percentage of spikes or inter-spike intervals violating the refractory period criterion after sorting, used as a quality indicator for the spike sorting process.
Number of putative neuronal units produced by the spike sorting process, counted at the end of the operation before downstream analysis.
Overall quality assessment of the spike sorting output based on unit separability, contamination, and stability; use a controlled categorical label.

spike_trains.reasoning: The spike_trains node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result descriptors: representation type, unit/channel dimensions, time base, binning or event encoding parameters, and quality indicators of the derived spike-train matrix. I excluded the spike sorting process settings and the raw signal properties because those belong upstream, and I excluded any later alignment or analysis outputs because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided repeating generic file descriptors already used for raw/filtered signals by focusing on the computed representation itself.

md_schema.descr: Type of computed spike-train representation produced from spike sorting output; examples include event times, binary raster, binned count matrix, or rate representation.
Number of detected units or channels represented in the spike train derivative, measured from the computed output matrix or event list.
Temporal bin size in milliseconds used to represent the spike trains if the derivative is binned; typical values may range from 1 to 100 ms depending on analysis goals.
Duration of the spike-train representation in seconds covered by the computed derivative, measured from the first to last represented event or time bin.
Number of discrete time bins or samples in the computed spike-train representation, depending on whether the output is binned or sampled on a regular time axis.
Units used for the temporal axis of the spike-train derivative, such as seconds or milliseconds, recorded as part of the computed representation.
Shape of the computed spike-train matrix expressed as a compact string such as units_by_time_bins or time_bins_by_units; use the actual dimensional ordering used in the derivative.
Quality assessment of the computed spike-train representation, summarizing whether the derivative is complete, consistent with source units, and suitable for downstream analysis.

lfp_feature_extraction.reasoning: The lfp_feature_extraction node is a Process, so I included only how the feature computation was performed: software identity, feature families selected, band definitions or epoch windows, aggregation settings, and output quality indicators. I excluded raw or filtered LFP file properties because those belong to Signal nodes, and I excluded the resulting feature table itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating generic software fields from earlier processes by using feature-extraction-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or algorithm used to compute LFP features from filtered field potentials; record the tool used at the feature-extraction step, such as a custom Python pipeline or a signal-analysis package.
Version of the feature-extraction software used in this process, recorded exactly as executed; example: 0.9.1.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used to run LFP feature extraction, recorded to support reproducibility of the process step.
Primary family of LFP features computed from the filtered traces during extraction; examples include spectral band power, event-locked averages, or trial-level summaries.

Frequency band definition used when computing spectral features from the filtered LFP, recorded as the analysis band applied in this step; example ranges may include delta, theta, alpha, beta, or gamma bands.
Time window in milliseconds used to compute event-locked or trial-locked LFP features, measured relative to the alignment event during extraction; example: -500 to 1500 ms.
Method used to aggregate LFP values into features during extraction, such as mean, median, peak-to-peak amplitude, or power spectral density integration.
Overall quality assessment of the extracted LFP features, summarizing whether the computed outputs are stable, complete, and suitable for downstream trial alignment or analysis.

lfp_features.reasoning: The lfp_features node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result metadata: feature table shape, feature families, trial/task epoch coverage, summary statistics, and output quality. I excluded feature-extraction parameters because those belong to the upstream lfp_feature_extraction Process, and I excluded raw/filtered signal properties because those belong to Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating generic file or software fields already used elsewhere in the DAG and focused on what downstream users need to interpret the feature table itself.

md_schema.descr: Format of the computed LFP feature table as stored for downstream use; record the table serialization used for the derivative output, such as CSV, Parquet, or HDF5.
Storage location or path for the computed LFP feature table, recorded as a string path or URI to the derivative artefact; example: s3://bucket/session1/lfp_features.parquet.
Size of the computed LFP feature table file in bytes measured after feature extraction and storage; this reflects the derivative artefact size rather than the source signal size.
Number of distinct LFP features included in the computed feature table, counted at the derivative output stage; typical values depend on the number of bands, epochs, and summaries extracted.
Number of trials represented in the LFP feature table, counted from the computed derivative output across behavioral task epochs.
Task or trial epoch labels represented in the LFP feature table, as used in the computed derivative; examples include baseline, stimulus, choice, or reward epochs.
Primary summary statistic used in the LFP feature table when features are aggregated across samples or trials; examples include mean, median, standard deviation, or area under the curve.
Overall quality assessment of the computed LFP feature table, summarizing completeness, consistency across trials, and suitability for downstream analysis; use a controlled categorical label.

trial_alignment.reasoning: The trial_alignment node is a Process, so I included only how alignment was performed: software identity, event anchors, pre/post windows, resampling or binning settings, and alignment quality indicators. I excluded source derivative properties because those belong upstream to spike_trains and lfp_features, and I excluded the aligned dataset itself because that belongs to the downstream aligned_neural_data Derivative. I also avoided repeating generic software fields used in other process nodes by naming alignment-specific parameters.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to align neural derivatives to behavioral events and stimulus timing; record the tool used at the trial_alignment step.
Version of the alignment software used in this process, recorded exactly as executed; example: 2.1.0.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used to run the trial alignment process, recorded to support reproducibility.
Primary behavioral or stimulus event used as the temporal anchor for trial alignment; examples include stimulus_onset, choice_time, or reward_delivery.
Time window in milliseconds before the alignment anchor included in each aligned trial segment, measured at the process step; example values may range from tens to hundreds of milliseconds.
Time window in milliseconds after the alignment anchor included in each aligned trial segment, measured at the process step; example values may range from hundreds to thousands of milliseconds.
Resampling rate in hertz used when neural derivatives are converted to a common trial-aligned time base, if applicable during the alignment process.
Maximum tolerated temporal mismatch in milliseconds between event timestamps and neural data during alignment; record the process tolerance used to accept or reject trial matches.
Overall quality assessment of the trial alignment process, summarizing whether event matching and windowing were successful and consistent across trials; use a controlled categorical label.

aligned_neural_data.reasoning: The aligned_neural_data node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-output descriptors: matrix shape, trial count, time axis definition, included modalities, event anchor, and output quality. I excluded the alignment parameters because those belong to the upstream trial_alignment Process, and I excluded raw feature or signal properties because those belong to upstream Derivative/Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any generic file descriptors already used for other data artefacts and kept the schema specific to the aligned trial-wise matrix.

md_schema.descr: Shape of the trial-aligned neural data matrix as stored in the derivative output, expressed in a compact form such as trials_by_features_by_time or trials_by_units_by_time; use the actual dimensional ordering used in the file.
Number of trials represented in the aligned neural data matrix, counted at the derivative output stage after trial alignment.
Temporal bin size in milliseconds used in the aligned neural matrix, if the data are discretized onto a common trial time base; typical values may range from 1 to 100 ms.
Event label used as the alignment anchor in the final aligned neural matrix, such as stimulus onset or choice time, recorded as represented in the derivative output.
Neural modalities represented in the aligned matrix, indicating whether spike-derived measures, LFP-derived measures, or both are present in the derivative output.
Total number of neural features or channels included in the aligned derivative matrix, counted after combining and aligning source representations.
Units used for the time axis of the aligned neural matrix, such as milliseconds relative to the alignment event; record the derivative's final time-base units.
Overall quality assessment of the aligned neural dataset, summarizing whether trial alignment is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for downstream multimodal analysis.

stimulus_parameters.reasoning: The stimulus_parameters node is an external Signal, so I included only raw external descriptor properties of the stimulus artefact: file format, storage location, session/trial count, timing resolution, parameter set identity, and technical quality of the external reference file. I excluded neural capture or process settings because those belong upstream or downstream in the neural workflow, and I excluded interpretation because this node represents the reference data itself rather than derived analysis. I also avoided repeating generic file or time-axis names already used for neural signal nodes by using stimulus-specific field names.

md_schema.descr: File format of the external stimulus parameters artefact as stored in the dataset; record the exact technical format used for the stimulus reference file, such as CSV, JSON, TSV, or HDF5.
Storage location or path for the stimulus parameters file, recorded as a string path or URI to the external reference artefact; example: s3://bucket/session1/stimulus_parameters.csv.
Size of the stimulus parameters file in bytes measured after storage; this reflects the external reference artefact size rather than neural signal size.
Number of trials or stimulus presentations described in the stimulus parameters artefact, counted from the external reference data.
Temporal resolution in milliseconds of stimulus timing descriptors in the external reference file, measured as the smallest recorded timing increment or sampling step.
Name of the stimulus parameter set or protocol identifier used to generate the external timing/reference file; example values may refer to a task-specific condition set.
Number of distinct stimulus settings or variables represented in the external stimulus parameters artefact, counted from the stored reference file.
Technical quality assessment of the external stimulus parameters artefact, such as whether the file is complete, readable, and suitable for alignment; use a controlled categorical label.

behavioral_annotations.reasoning: The behavioral_annotations node is an external Signal, so I included only artefact-level descriptors of the annotation file: file format, storage location, annotation vocabulary, trial count, timing resolution, and technical quality. I excluded neural capture or analysis parameters because those belong to the electrophysiology or process nodes, and I excluded interpreted outcomes because the node represents the external annotation source itself. I also avoided duplicating any already-generated generic file fields by using behavior-specific names.

md_schema.descr: File format of the external behavioral annotations artefact as stored in the dataset; record the exact technical format used for the annotation file, such as CSV, JSON, TSV, or HDF5.
Storage location or path for the behavioral annotations file, recorded as a string path or URI to the external annotation artefact; example: s3://bucket/session1/behavior_annotations.csv.
Size of the behavioral annotations file in bytes measured after storage; this reflects the external annotation artefact size rather than neural data size.
Number of trials or annotated task events represented in the behavioral annotations artefact, counted from the external reference data.
Temporal resolution in milliseconds of the behavioral event annotations, measured as the smallest recorded timing increment or sampling step in the annotation file.
Name of the event or label vocabulary used in the behavioral annotations file, such as task-specific choice labels, performance codes, or event labels.
Number of distinct annotation labels or event categories represented in the behavioral annotation artefact, counted from the stored file.
Technical quality assessment of the external behavioral annotations artefact, such as whether the file is complete, readable, and suitable for alignment; use a controlled categorical label.

multimodal_integration.reasoning: The multimodal_integration node is a Process, so I included only how the integration was performed: software identity, join strategy, key fields used for merging, handling of missing/duplicate trials, and output-quality indicators. I excluded the properties of the input aligned neural data and external annotation files because those belong to upstream nodes, and I excluded the final task dataset contents because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating generic software fields from earlier processes by using integration-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to combine aligned neural data with stimulus parameters and behavioral annotations; record the tool used at the multimodal_integration step.
Version of the integration software used in this process, recorded exactly as executed; example: 1.4.0.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used to run the multimodal integration process, recorded to support reproducibility.
Name of the primary key used to merge aligned neural data with stimulus and behavioral tables during integration; examples include trial_id or session_trial_index.
Strategy used to merge the input tables during integration, recorded at the process step; examples include inner join, left join, or outer join.
Rule used to handle trials missing from one or more input modalities during integration, such as dropping, imputing, or flagging incomplete rows.
Rule used to handle duplicate trial records encountered during multimodal integration, recorded as the process-level resolution strategy.
Overall quality assessment of the multimodal integration process, summarizing whether merged rows are complete, consistent, and suitable for downstream analysis; use a controlled categorical label.

task_dataset.reasoning: The task_dataset node is a Derivative, so I included only computed integrated-dataset descriptors: table format, storage location, row/column counts, source modality composition, and dataset quality. I excluded the integration procedure because that belongs to the upstream multimodal_integration Process, and I excluded any decision-analysis outputs because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating generic file fields already used for other artefacts by using task-dataset-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Format of the integrated task dataset as stored for downstream use; record the serialization used for the derivative output, such as CSV, Parquet, or HDF5.
Storage location or path for the integrated task dataset, recorded as a string path or URI to the derivative artefact; example: s3://bucket/session1/task_dataset.parquet.
Size of the integrated task dataset file in bytes measured after multimodal integration and storage; this reflects the derivative artefact size rather than source input sizes.
Number of rows or trial-level records in the integrated task dataset, counted at the derivative output stage after combining neural, stimulus, and behavioral data.
Number of columns or variables in the integrated task dataset, counted in the final derivative table after multimodal integration.

Source data modalities represented in the integrated task dataset, indicating which inputs were combined into the derivative output; this dataset is expected to include neural, stimulus, and behavioral information.
Number of trials represented in the integrated task dataset, counted from the final derivative table after multimodal integration.

Overall quality assessment of the integrated task dataset, summarizing completeness, row consistency, and suitability for downstream metadata generation or analysis; use a controlled categorical label.

metadata_table_building.reasoning: The metadata_table_building node is a Process, so I included only how the table was constructed: software identity, table-building rules, schema/coding decisions, aggregation or normalization settings, and output-quality indicators. I excluded the integrated dataset properties because those belong to the upstream task_dataset Derivative, and I excluded the resulting metadata table contents because those belong to the downstream metadata_table Derivative. I also avoided repeating generic software fields by using metadata-table-specific process names and focused on reproducible table-construction parameters.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to convert the integrated task dataset into a structured metadata table; record the tool used at the metadata_table_building step.
Version of the metadata-building software used in this process, recorded exactly as executed; example: 1.0.0.
Repository, script package, or pipeline name used to build the metadata table, recorded to support reproducibility of the process step.
Version identifier of the metadata table schema applied during table construction; use this to track the exact column layout and coding rules used in the process.
Primary unit represented by each row in the constructed metadata table, such as trial, session, or unit, recorded at the table-building step.
Method used to normalize or standardize values during metadata table construction, such as z-scoring, min-max scaling, unit conversion, or categorical harmonization.
Policy used to handle missing fields during metadata table construction, such as leaving nulls, imputing values, or creating explicit missingness flags.

Overall quality assessment of the table-building process, summarizing whether the constructed metadata table is internally consistent, schema-compliant, and ready for downstream use; use a controlled categorical label.

metadata_table.reasoning: The metadata_table node is a Derivative, so I included only the properties of the final table itself: serialization format, storage location, table dimensions, row granularity, and quality/completeness of the computed metadata artefact. I excluded table-building parameters because those belong to the upstream metadata_table_building Process, and I excluded the scientific content fields that would duplicate upstream session, neural, stimulus, or behavior metadata already represented elsewhere in the DAG. I also avoided repeating generic file descriptors from prior signal and dataset nodes by using metadata-table-specific names.

md_schema.descr: Format of the computed metadata table as stored for downstream use; record the serialization used for the derivative output, such as CSV, Parquet, TSV, or HDF5.
Storage location or path for the computed metadata table, recorded as a string path or URI to the derivative artefact; example: s3://bucket/session1/metadata_table.parquet.
Size of the computed metadata table file in bytes measured after construction and storage; this reflects the derivative artefact size rather than source dataset size.
Number of rows in the computed metadata table, counted at the final derivative output stage; rows are typically session-level, trial-level, or unit-level records depending on the schema.
Number of columns or fields in the computed metadata table, counted in the final derivative artefact after table construction.
Primary unit represented by each row in the metadata table, as encoded in the final derivative; examples include session, trial, or unit.

Assessment of which major content categories are represented in the metadata table, such as recording sessions, task conditions, neural features, and behavioral variables, measured as a completeness statement for the derivative output.

Overall quality assessment of the computed metadata table, summarizing whether it is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for downstream analysis or dataset release; use a controlled categorical label.

decision_analysis.reasoning: The decision_analysis node is a Process, so I included only how the statistical analysis was performed: analysis software identity, model family, predictor/outcome definitions, correction settings, and summary quality indicators.
